source_neutral.procedure: The proposed onboarding redesign is represented as a set of removable elements with explicit dependencies among them. Instructions, defaults, screens and assistance are candidate categories of element, not supplied facts about the proposal. The working object is a configuration of omissions relative to a fixed reference prototype; reducing that configuration means restoring elements that had been omitted. The procedure assumes that valid variants can be built and tested repeatedly with comparable users and tasks. Before testing, the definition of activation, the permitted assistance, the observation window, the repeatability criteria, and the criteria for success, failure and unresolved outcomes are fixed. Two preconditions are established first: activation is reproducible in the reference prototype, and activation failure is reproducible in at least one valid omission configuration. If either cannot be established, the reduction is stopped and the reference flow or test reliability is investigated before any necessity conclusion is drawn. Otherwise the failing omission set is iteratively reduced until no tested reduction still produces failure, followed by single-element restoration checks at the endpoint.
source_neutral.action: Partition the omission set that produces activation failure. Test subsets of the omissions and their complements by restoring the other omitted elements, while holding the remaining flow, task and environment fixed. Keep a smaller omission set when, and only when, it still meets the predefined activation-failure criterion. Repartition and refine until no tested reduction preserves failure. Allocate participants comparably and control prior exposure so that learning is not mistaken for an effect of restoring an element. Classify structurally invalid variants and ambiguous or inconsistent outcomes as unresolved, not as activation failures. At the endpoint, test restoring each remaining omitted element individually. Where unresolved outcomes or a declared testing budget prevent completion, report a provisional reduced set. Where feasible, repeat the reduction starting from other failing omission sets or using other partition orders. For suspected interactions between two omissions, test four conditions against the same fixed remainder, using valid variants: neither omitted, each one omitted alone, and both omitted.
source_neutral.observables: For each omission configuration, record whether it preserves activation failure, restores activation, or remains unresolved. Outcome evidence is prototype task completion and funnel events. Observed errors and session notes can indicate where users become blocked, but do not by themselves determine necessity. In the interaction comparisons, two patterns are sought: (a) omissions that are each tolerated individually but block activation when made jointly, indicating that the corresponding elements may provide alternative support; (b) a failure that disappears after an additional omission, indicating context dependence or nonmonotonic behavior. These are proposed observations to look for, not established findings.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: A retained failing omission set identifies removals that are sufficient to reproduce activation failure under the defined test. A verified endpoint set, in which the set reproducibly fails and each single restoration reproducibly succeeds, additionally shows that restoring any one of its omitted elements removes that failure in the tested configuration. A set containing a single element supports conditional necessity of that element with the reference remainder held fixed. A set containing multiple elements does not establish that each omitted element is individually necessary, because jointly removing alternative routes can block activation even when either route alone suffices. Different reduced sets and interaction results can therefore support priorities stated for combinations and contexts, in place of a simple independent feature ranking.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: individual removable elements of the redesign (candidate categories: instructions, defaults, screens, assistance); dependencies between elements; omission configurations defined relative to a fixed reference prototype; subsets of an omission set and their complements; the fixed remainder of flow, task and environment; and three outcome classes (activation success, activation failure, unresolved). Relationships: each omission configuration is linked to an outcome class; a reduced set is related to its parent set by restoration of some omitted elements; endpoint sets are related to their single-restoration variants; pairs of omissions are related through the four-condition comparison (neither, each alone, both), which distinguishes elements that may substitute for one another from failures that depend on context or behave nonmonotonically; endpoints from different starting sets or partition orders are compared with one another. The question of which elements are needed is addressed through sets of omissions sufficient for failure and single-element restorations that remove it; the question of what prevents a simple ranking is addressed through the multi-element sets, differing endpoints and interaction comparisons.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Specified follow-up: (1) if reproducible activation in the reference or reproducible failure in at least one valid omission configuration cannot be established, investigate the reference flow or test reliability before drawing necessity conclusions; (2) where feasible, repeat the reduction from other failing omission sets or with other partition orders; (3) follow up suspected interactions by testing neither, either and both omissions against the same fixed remainder, using valid variants. No further follow-up is specified.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions: valid variants must be buildable and repeatably testable with comparable users and tasks; activation, permitted assistance, observation window, repeatability criteria and outcome classes must be defined in advance; the remaining flow, task and environment are held fixed; participant allocation is comparable and prior exposure is controlled; interaction tests use valid variants. Stopping rules: stop the reduction and investigate the reference flow or test reliability if reproducible activation in the reference or reproducible failure in at least one valid omission configuration cannot be established; stop with a test-relative result of single-restoration minimality when, and only when, the current set reproducibly fails and every single restoration reproducibly succeeds; otherwise report a provisional reduced set when unresolved outcomes or a declared testing budget prevent completion. Scope limits: the result concerns the tested users, tasks, implementation, environment and outcome criteria, and does not establish population-wide necessity. The procedure minimizes failure-producing omissions, not the successful redesign itself. Dependencies may prevent independent removal of elements. Participant variability, learning, unresolved outcomes and environmental changes can weaken reproducibility. The order of reduction can select different endpoints. Single-restoration checks establish that no single restoration preserves failure, not that the omission set is the globally smallest; nonmonotonic interactions can conceal smaller failing sets. Reproducible failure does not uniquely identify its causal mechanism. An element conditionally required in one configuration may be dispensable in another.
